categories.main_business_segments: Popular, Inc. is a diversified financial holding company operating primarily through two main segments: Puerto Rico operations (serving 77% of assets and 81% of deposits) through Banco Popular de Puerto Rico, offering retail, mortgage, and commercial banking, auto and equipment leasing, investment banking, and insurance services; and Mainland United States operations through Popular Bank in New York, New Jersey, and Florida, providing retail, mortgage, and commercial banking along with investment and insurance services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company relies on digital banking platforms, online deposit gathering systems, and core financial transaction processing services. Popular has acquired certain information technology and related assets from Evertec to service key banking channels. The company is undergoing a significant multi-year technological transformation to enhance digital capabilities, modernize technology infrastructure, and implement agile business processes across the organization.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers include retail consumers, commercial businesses, and government entities. Key markets are Puerto Rico (primary market with largest retail banking franchise), New York, New Jersey, Florida, U.S. Virgin Islands, and British Virgin Islands. The company serves residential and commercial real estate sectors, hospitality, healthcare, and other industries, with significant exposure to Puerto Rico government entities and municipalities.
categories.geographic_coverage: Operations are concentrated in Puerto Rico (77% of assets, 81% of deposits, 78% of revenues as of December 31, 2023), with secondary presence in the Mainland United States including New York, New Jersey, and Florida. The company also operates in the U.S. Virgin Islands and British Virgin Islands, and offers financial products on a national scale in the U.S. market through online platforms.
categories.supply_chain_position: Popular operates as a downstream financial services provider, directly serving end consumers and businesses through retail and commercial banking. The company depends on upstream relationships with the Federal Reserve, Federal Home Loan Bank, and FDIC for liquidity and deposit insurance. It also relies on third-party service providers, particularly Evertec, for core financial transaction processing and technology infrastructure.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company's primary strategic focus is a broad-based multi-year technological and business process transformation launched in 2022, targeting a 14% return on tangible common equity by end of 2025. Key initiatives include expanding digital capabilities, modernizing technology foundation, implementing agile business processes, enhancing customer digital experience, and improving operational efficiency. The company is also transitioning away from dependency on Evertec for certain services.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through net interest income from lending activities (commercial, mortgage, consumer, construction, and lease financing), deposit-based banking services, and fees from investment banking, broker-dealer, insurance services, and auto/equipment leasing. The company also generates revenue from loan sales and securitizations, with deposits serving as the primary low-cost funding source.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In Puerto Rico, primary competitors include locally-based commercial banks and large U.S. and foreign banks with operations there. The company also competes with credit unions, brokerage firms, mortgage companies, insurance companies, and non-traditional financial service providers. In the Mainland U.S., Popular faces competition from numerous community, regional, and national banking institutions in New York, New Jersey, and Florida markets. Popular ranks among the 50 largest U.S. bank holding companies by assets.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2023, Popular had consolidated assets of $70.8 billion, total deposits of $63.6 billion, and stockholders' equity of $5.1 billion. The company is a large accelerated filer with approximately 72.3 million shares outstanding. Market capitalization was approximately $4.3 billion as of June 30, 2023. The company has experienced gradual recovery following Puerto Rico's economic challenges and is pursuing growth through transformation initiatives and selective acquisitions.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Popular emphasizes its position as the largest financial institution based in Puerto Rico with the largest retail banking franchise in the territory. The company differentiates through comprehensive product offerings across retail, commercial, and investment banking; personalized banking services; high service levels to enhance customer loyalty; digital innovation and enhanced customer experience; and deep local market knowledge and relationships, particularly in Puerto Rico. The company also emphasizes employee development, diversity and inclusion, and community engagement as part of its value proposition.
